chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about tayammum, so he struck the earth with his two hands, then raised them and shook them off, then wiped with them his forehead and his two palms once.

As for the report which al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Uthman, from سماعة, who said: I asked him, 'How is tayammum?' So he placed his hand upon the earth and wiped with it his face and his forearms up to the elbows.

He only intended by that the ruling, not the act itself, because when he wipes the outer side of the palm, it is as though he had washed his forearms in wudu (ablution). Thus, by wiping the two palms in tayammum, there is obtained for him the ruling corresponding to washing the two forearms in wudu (ablution), and this indicates that he did not intend the actual wiping of the forearms.

key_terms.جَبْهَتَهُ: his forehead, the part of the face wiped in tayammum
key_terms.ذِرَاعَيْهِ: his two forearms, mentioned in the cited report up to the elbows
key_terms.كَفَّيْهِ: his two palms, which are wiped in tayammum
key_terms.ٱلتَّيَمُّمِ: dry ablution performed with earth when water cannot be used
key_terms.ٱلْحُكْمَ: the legal ruling or juridical equivalence intended in the explanation
key_terms.ٱلْفِعْلَ: the actual physical act, distinguished here from the ruling
key_terms.ٱلْمِرْفَقَيْنِ: the two elbows, the endpoint mentioned for the forearms
key_terms.ٱلْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), used here as the point of comparison

ai.seo_question: How is tayammum performed according to Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the method of tayammum as striking the earth with both hands, shaking them lightly, and wiping the forehead and palms once. It also addresses a report mentioning the forearms, explaining that it refers to the legal equivalence in ruling rather than the literal act of wiping the forearms.
